summary.intent: Add new release targets to the Callisto artifact build matrix and related config, CI, docs, and installer mapping as PR D, stacked on PR C.
summary.outcome: Applied the release target edits, ran workflow contract checks, zizmor and behavior tests, then ran full `just ci` which passed (exit=0). Added a changeset, committed, pushed, and opened PR D stacked on PR C.

repo: Release targets are enumerated in several places: the artifact build matrix/config/build script, the CI preflight matrix (.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml), README targets, docs/architecture/release.md, and the installer platform mapping tests, so adding a target requires coordinated edits across all of them.

The setup-callisto action installer (.github/actions/setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh) has a platform mapping with an extraction/mapping test that has per-platform cases which must be extended for new targets.
CI validation includes workflow contract checks, zizmor (GitHub Actions security linting) and installer behavior tests, all run via `just ci`.
The repo uses changesets, so release-affecting PRs need a changeset entry.
Work is done in git worktrees under .claude/worktrees (e.g. smoke-main) and uses stacked PRs (D on C).

code.finding: Installer maps platforms to release artifacts; it was read to determine how new targets need to be mapped and tested.

workflow: Using throwaway scripts in /tmp (edit_targets.py, targets_check.sh, targets_ci.sh) to apply edits and run verification kept the multi-file change reproducible.
Confirming the CI exit code explicitly before shipping gave a verified basis for opening the PR.
Grepping for every place that enumerates targets before editing helps avoid missing one.

open_items: PR D is stacked on PR C and depends on it merging first; it may need rebasing after PR C lands.
